summary.headline: ideaForge Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR68.6 crore from INR12.8 crore, with EBITDA positive at INR4.3 crore and gross margin at 49%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR68.6 crore versus INR12.8 crore a year ago, and the company reported positive EBITDA of INR4.3 crore against a negative INR15.1 crore in Q1 FY26. Gross margin fell to 49% from 61.7%, which management attributed to a 60:40 product mix versus the usual 70:30. Management said it delivered over 20% of the opening order book of above INR300 crore and has INR256.8 crore left to deliver by Q3. Management also highlighted a INR500 crore QIP, a Letter of Intent for up to INR151 crore for YETI, and a larger defence procurement pipeline, but gave no order-inflow or US revenue numbers.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Management said the order book is heavier towards defence but did not disclose the split. EW-resilient products carry higher margins than civil, which management cited as a reason for the Q1 gross margin dip.

segments.name: Civil / homeland security
segments.commentary: Civil revenue is from homeland security customers and private customers; management did not give a split. Civil run-rate procurement is expected to pick up in Q3 and Q4.

guidance_outlook: Blended gross margin for FY27 expected to stay in the 50%-55% range; management said the quarterly mix would vary.
Remaining INR256.8 crore order book to be delivered by Q3 FY27, subject to customer timelines.
No revenue guidance given; management does not forecast top-line numbers.
Run-rate defence and civil procurement expected to fructify in Q3 and Q4 after the Army commanders' financial powers were enhanced.
Fast-track procurement RFPs expected in H2 FY27; management said at least a couple could convert this year, while some may slip to FY28.
Revenue from the new opportunities expected to show up in the order book from Q1 FY28 and in deliveries over the subsequent 18 months, per the CFO.
capex_capacity: No capex plan beyond regular product development; no new factory planned.
Current operations run on a single shift; the company can move to three shifts in the same space.
Supply pressure on thermal cameras and electronics has caused some delivery timeline slippage, though management says there is no current impact on customer commitments.

YETI received a Letter of Intent for up to INR151 crore from the Technology Development Board under the RDI scheme, released against development milestones. The first technical demonstrator completed a tethered hover test; the second is in design.
Q6 V2 GEO received DGCA Type Certification; six UAV platforms are now type certified.
demand_pricing: Indian Army fast-track procurement of INR20,000 crore of drones is in the pipeline; one opportunity is at RFP stage (hybrid ZOLT, ISR, per management). Budget per fast-track case is up to INR2,000 crore.
Defence Acquisition Council cleared INR52,000 crore of capital acquisition proposals, including a jet-based kamikaze drone and a naval shipborne UAS.
Ministry of Defence nearly doubled operational procurement limits for field commanders under the Delegation of Financial Powers 2026.
A 2,715-unit logistics drone RFI was referenced by analysts; management said it focuses on altitude and it is at RFI stage only.
US: JV with a partner being operationalised; Blue sUAS certification in progress and needed for US federal/defence business. Management cited a live US programme of about USD30 million.
International: NFR unit orders received from partners in South America and Africa; partnerships being sought in Europe and Middle East.
Indigenisation: about 20%-22% of revenue is import-substituted; international content across the product line is about 60%-65%, per the CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the disconnect in government order inflow despite funding and field testing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said large fast-track opportunities follow a longer cycle from DPB approval to order, while run-rate revenue business typically starts in Q3 and Q4 unless an EP-linked programme is running.

qa_highlights.question: How does YETI compare with the logistics drone RFI and BluJ Aero's platform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said YETI is designed for 6,500 m takeoff altitude with up to 200 kg payload and is, in its view, the only such platform it has found. It also said the RFI is at an early stage and the opportunity size cannot yet be estimated.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company's pipeline of FTP and run-rate orders likely to convert in FY27, and how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some FTP programmes may slip to FY28 but at least a couple could convert this year. It did not quantify the expected order inflow.

qa_highlights.question: Are there supply chain constraints in delivering the order book by Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said thermal camera and electronics supply are under pressure with timeline delays, but there is no current expectation of delivery delays against customer timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin pressure continue during order book execution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 49% Q1 margin reflected the 60:40 product mix against a usual 70:30, and it does not expect a material move from the 50%-55% FY27 blended guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Are the combat drone programmes still R&D or are procurement opportunities visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said combat development (air-launched effects, ZOLT fuel-hybrid) is progressing with partners on long-range strike and loitering munitions, and the company bid for the ZOLT hybrid ISR RFP. It will not bid on every category.

risks_watch: Gross margin trajectory versus 50%-55% FY27 guidance as product mix changes quarter to quarter.
Supply chain delays in thermal cameras and electronics affecting Q3 delivery of INR256.8 crore order book.
Timing of fast-track RFP conversions and possible FY28 slippage.
US Blue sUAS certification and JV operationalisation timing.
Competitive pressure from larger defence players and new logistics drone entrants; the company gave no market-share estimate.
Quarterly results may vary with opportunity cycles, product mix, delivery schedules and customer acceptance, per management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the procurement pipeline and long-term strategy, but guarded on specifics: management declined to quantify order inflow, market share, the order book split, US market size, and the non-order-book revenue bridge, pointing to case-by-case timing.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 marked a steady start to the year, supported by continued execution and advancement across key strategic developmental programs.
For example, YETI, in my opinion, is the only platform in the world from whatever we have searched that is designed to take off at 6,500 meters takeoff altitude.
So, we do not expect that number to be shifting on an overall basis.

adds.what: No new factory or capacity expansion planned; only regular product development capex
